title: wallet-web: crate skeleton, config, init, fail-closed startup
description:
Create the `wallet-web` binary crate: config, `init`, fail-closed startup.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.0, §6c.1, §6c.6. Posture: ADR-0028.
The spec is authoritative and complete — follow it rather than improvising.

Required:
1. New workspace member `wallet-web` (binary). A CLIENT of walletd over HTTP with a bearer token,
   exactly like wallet-cli. NEVER opens client.db or journal.db (daemon holds exclusive locks).
2. Bind address is HARD-CODED to 127.0.0.1 — only the port is configurable (default 9737). Do not
   add a bind-address config option: it would let 0.0.0.0 satisfy this spec while breaking the
   fixed exposure posture.
3. The daemon URL must be http:// and its host an IP LITERAL in 127.0.0.0/8 or ::1. Reject DNS
   names outright -- including `localhost`, which resolves but is not a literal and can be
   repointed -- and reject non-http schemes. Fail startup otherwise, or a
   typo ships the full-access bearer token in plaintext to a remote host.
4. `wallet-web.toml`, written 0600 with the mode RE-ASSERTED after write (mirror
   wallet-daemon/src/config.rs). Holds: port, daemon URL, token path, Argon2id PHC hash, session
   idle/absolute timeouts, and `public_origin` (explicit scheme+host+port, NOT derived from Host).
5. `wallet-web init`: no-echo prompt, confirm, enforce a 12-char minimum, reject >1024-byte input
   BEFORE hashing, hash with Argon2id at pinned params (m=19456 KiB, t=2, p=1), write config.
6. Server REFUSES TO START with no hash, a malformed PHC string, or params below those minimums.
   Fail closed: no default credential, no "auth disabled until configured", no setup page.

Tests: init writes 0600; startup fails with no hash / malformed PHC / weak params; startup rejects
a non-loopback daemon URL (there is NO bind-address test -- the address is a hard-coded
constant, not configuration); passwords under 12 chars rejected;
oversized input rejected before hashing.

Scope guard: no routes, no auth logic, no templates here. Do NOT touch the daemon. No JS toolchain.
Greenfield: no backwards-compat or migration code.
7. Structured `tracing` logging is initialised at startup. The level comes from the RUST_LOG
   environment variable, NOT from wallet-web.toml -- the plan's config inventory is deliberately
   closed, and adding keys to it is out of scope. NEVER log the
   password, the session token, the daemon bearer token, or a full invoice -- at any level.
8. ADD `wallet-web` TO THE NIX BUILD. `flake.nix`'s `rustSrc` filters the source to an explicit
   list of the five existing crates; adding a workspace member without adding its directory there
   leaves `nix build` seeing a member that is not in the filtered source, and the build breaks.
   Add "wallet-web" to that `paths` list in the same change that adds the crate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] wallet-web builds as a workspace member and starts, serving nothing yet.
- [ ] The bind address is a hard-coded loopback constant: no config key can change it (the config struct has no bind-address field at all).
- [ ] Startup EXITS NON-ZERO with a clear message when any of these hold: no password hash configured; malformed PHC string; Argon2id params below the pinned minimums (m=19456, t=2, p=1); daemon URL not http:// literal loopback.
- [ ] wallet-web init writes the config 0600, verified after a run under umask 000.
- [ ] init rejects a password under 12 chars, and rejects >1024-byte input BEFORE hashing.
- [ ] Every criterion above is covered by a test that runs under the default cargo test.
- [ ] Startup initialises structured tracing at the RUST_LOG-selected level (NOT a wallet-web.toml
      key -- the plan's config inventory is deliberately closed).
- [ ] A grep of the tree finds no log statement carrying the password, session token, bearer token,
      or a full invoice. Runtime log-capture for the AUTH path belongs to br-nfz and for
      invoice-bearing money paths to br-t8f; the final repository-wide audit is br-4yz. This bead
      builds no routes and no auth logic, so it cannot exercise them.
- [ ] Startup rejects an Argon2i AND an Argon2d PHC string even when m/t/p look strong. The plan
      fixes the ALGORITHM as Argon2id; testing only malformed strings and weak parameters leaves a
      strong-looking wrong-family hash passing every listed check.
- [ ] Oversized password input is proven to reach NO hashing operation at all, rather than merely
      being rejected after the fact.
- [ ] `nix build` succeeds with the new crate present, proving flake.nix's rustSrc paths were
      updated alongside the workspace members list.
- [ ] The daemon-URL test names `http://localhost:9736` explicitly and asserts it is REJECTED. A
      suite that only rejects e.g. `http://192.168.1.5` passes while an implementation that
      resolves-and-accepts `localhost` ships — and `localhost` is the URL an operator would most
      naturally type, which is why item 3 was sharpened to exclude it.

title: wallet-web: Argon2id login, sessions, CSRF, security headers
description:
`wallet-web` authentication: Argon2id login, sessions, CSRF, security headers.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.2 AND the Settings paragraph in §6c.5 (both
authoritative — implement exactly). ADR-0028.
This is the ONLY control protecting full CLI parity including /v1/recover. Treat it as such.

Required (each of these was a review finding; none is optional):
1. Every route requires a session EXCEPT `GET /login`, `POST /login`, `GET /healthz`. There is NO
   static-asset exemption — inline the login page's CSS/JS into that page.
2. Cookie: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, HOST-ONLY (no Domain). `Secure` is set iff the
   configured `public_origin` scheme is https — NEVER from the request and never from
   X-Forwarded-Proto. The sidecar terminates no TLS, so a request-derived condition can never fire
   and the cookie behind an HTTPS proxy would be permanently non-Secure and stealable.
3. Session record is `token -> {created_at, last_seen, csrf_secret}`. The CSRF secret is a SEPARATE
   256-bit CSPRNG value; the session cookie must never be echoed into HTML.
4. Regenerate BOTH values on every successful login regardless of any presented cookie (fixation).
5. Sliding 4h idle + absolute 24h, enforced server-side every request. Polling and /healthz are
   PASSIVE: they validate but must NOT update last_seen, or 3s polling keeps a tab authorized for
   the full 24h and the idle timeout never fires.
6. A loopback peer address does NOT authenticate. X-Forwarded-For is not trusted for anything.
7. Rate limiting: global, checked and incremented ATOMICALLY BEFORE any hashing so concurrent
   attempts cannot slip past the 5-failure boundary. Argon2 on a bounded blocking pool; no lock
   held across hashing or backoff, so logins cannot starve authenticated requests.
8. CSRF: session's csrf_secret in a hidden field on every mutating request, constant-time compared.
   `POST /login` is exempt from the token (no session yet) but NOT from the origin check. Origin
   (or Referer fallback) must match `public_origin` EXACTLY (scheme + host + effective port). A
   Referer is a FULL URL (`https://host/form`), so PARSE AND NORMALIZE it to its origin triple
   before comparing -- never string-compare the whole value, which rejects every legitimate
   request. Reject a Referer carrying credentials, and reject malformed values. A request with
   neither header is rejected.
9. Logout is POST with CSRF and clears the server-side entry.
10. Security headers on EVERY response including login, redirects, errors and /healthz. The CSP
    MUST carry a fresh per-response CSPRNG nonce on `script-src` and `style-src`
    (`default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<n>'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-<n>';
    frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'`) and the login page's inlined <style>/<script> must
    carry it. A bare `default-src 'self'` does NOT authorize inline elements and would silently
    block the login assets item 1 requires to be inlined.
11. Session timeouts are the security contract and configuration may only ever TIGHTEN them:
    values above the 4h idle / 24h absolute ceilings, or unparseable values, FAIL STARTUP rather
    than silently widening the only mitigation ADR-0028 relies on.

Tests: see spec §6c.7. Identify them by what they assert, NOT by item number -- the numbering has
gone stale twice across revisions. This bead owns: security headers, the login baseline, loopback
not authenticating, session expiry (including that continuous polling does not extend it),
session/CSRF regeneration, the CSRF and origin rejections, rate limiting, and logout replay.


Scope guard: no step-up (ADR-0028 decided against — do not reintroduce), no multi-user, no roles.
Never log the password, session token, or bearer token. Ownership split so the two cannot contradict: THIS bead owns the auth MIDDLEWARE and the routes that exist at this stage. The single EXHAUSTIVE route manifest, which must also cover routes added by later beads, belongs to br-4yz.
12. A DEDICATED ORIGIN is required. Mount at the root and set a HOST-ONLY cookie (no Domain
    attribute). Co-hosting the wallet under a path on an origin shared with another application is
    UNSUPPORTED and must be documented as such in the crate docs: no cookie attribute, SameSite
    setting, or Origin check isolates two apps on one origin -- the neighbour can fetch
    authenticated pages, read the CSRF field out of the HTML, and submit actions.
13. `Cache-Control: no-store` on every authenticated response, so balances never land in a shared
    cache or come back via the back button after logout.
14. Log failed logins and rate-limiter engagement at `warn`, carrying NO password material. The
    password is the only control in front of /v1/recover, so a brute-force attempt must leave a
    trace an operator can see -- a limiter that silently absorbs an attack is invisible.
15. A failed login must be INDISTINGUISHABLE regardless of cause: identical HTTP status,
    identical response body, identical timing class, and NO session cookie set. Never reveal
    whether a password was merely wrong versus any other failure, and never expose a
    user-existence signal (there is one account, so any such distinction is pure leak).

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every user-facing string this bead renders --
including login, settings and error text: never "risk engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb,
"curated", or "anonymous".
16. OWN THE SETTINGS / CHANGE-PASSWORD FLOW (plan §6c.5 assigns it to the auth work; no bead
    carried it). The full contract: change password ONLY; the OLD password must be re-entered; the
    config is rewritten ATOMICALLY and re-asserted to 0600; the in-memory verifier is replaced ONLY
    AFTER that write succeeds; the ACTING SESSION SURVIVES and every other session is invalidated.
    This flow rewrites the credential file guarding /v1/recover: swapping the verifier before a
    failed write either locks the operator out or leaves the old password live, and skipping
    old-password re-entry turns any hijacked session into a permanent credential takeover.
17. STRUCTURAL: session creation takes an ALREADY-VERIFIED principal, so credential checking is a
    separate step from session establishment (plan §6c.9a). This is what ADR-0028's "accepts a
    second credential type without rework" reduces to. It has no behavioural test by design; it is
    a code-shape constraint, and coupling the two would satisfy every other criterion here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] THE BASELINE: the correct password authenticates and establishes a working session, and a
      wrong password does not, failing indistinguishably. Every other criterion here assumes
      login works; this is the one that proves it.
- [ ] Every route except GET /login, POST /login and GET /healthz returns 401/redirect without a session, asserted by enumerating the route table rather than a hand-listed sample.
- [ ] An unauthenticated request from 127.0.0.1 is still rejected: loopback is not authentication.
- [ ] A session expires after 4h idle AND after 24h absolute even under continuous use, and continuous 3s polling does NOT extend it.
- [ ] Session and CSRF values are both regenerated on login, and the hidden CSRF field never equals the cookie value.
- [ ] A mutating request is rejected when the CSRF token is absent or wrong, when Origin mismatches public_origin, and when both Origin and Referer are absent. A full-URL Referer on the correct origin is ACCEPTED, proving it is parsed to an origin triple rather than string-compared.
- [ ] Login rate limiting engages after 5 consecutive failures, resets on success, holds under concurrent attempts, and does not starve authenticated requests while throttling.
- [ ] A configured session timeout above the 4h idle / 24h absolute ceiling fails startup instead of widening it.
- [ ] The CSP carries a fresh per-response nonce, the login page's inline style/script carry it, and the required security headers appear on every response class including redirects, errors and /healthz.
- [ ] An authenticated session can change the password, and doing so invalidates every other session.
- [ ] The session cookie is host-only (no Domain attribute) and the app mounts at the root.
- [ ] Crate docs state that path co-hosting on a shared origin is unsupported, and why.
- [ ] Every authenticated response carries Cache-Control: no-store; a back-button navigation after
      logout does not reveal a cached balance page.
- [ ] A failed login emits a warn-level event; the limiter engaging emits one; neither carries the
      password, the session token, or the bearer token.
- [ ] Log capture over the AUTH path proves no password, session token, or bearer token appears at
      any level, on both a successful and a failed login.
- [ ] The backoff SCHEDULE is exact, not merely 'exponential': failures 1-4 undelayed; the 5th and
      each subsequent consecutive failure sleeps min(2^(n-5) s, 30s) -- 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30...
      Assert the table AND the 30s cap. A microsecond-scale curve satisfies 'exponential' and
      protects nothing. Reset to zero on success.
- [ ] Restarting the sidecar invalidates every session (the documented revoke-all), asserted by
      reusing a pre-restart cookie and being refused.
- [ ] A Referer carrying credentials (user:pass@host) is REJECTED, and a malformed Referer is
      REJECTED rather than parsed leniently.
- [ ] Origin matching compares the EFFECTIVE PORT: a request from the right host on the wrong port
      is rejected.
- [ ] POST /login with a mismatched Origin, and with neither Origin nor Referer, is rejected --
      login is exempt from the CSRF token but NOT from the origin check.
- [ ] X-Forwarded-For is provably ignored: forging it changes neither rate limiting nor any
      access decision.
- [ ] A wrong password and any other login failure are byte-identical in status and body, and
      neither sets a cookie.
- [ ] Every user-facing string this bead adds conforms to the copy canon.
- [ ] The COMPLETE Set-Cookie contract is asserted, not just host-only: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict,
      Path=/, no Domain, and Secure present iff `public_origin` is https -- asserted with an http
      public_origin AND an https one.
- [ ] X-Forwarded-Proto is forged in BOTH directions and provably changes the Secure flag not at
      all. Deriving Secure from the request is the precise reverse-proxy failure the plan warns
      about, and a host-only-only test cannot see it.
- [ ] The session token and the CSRF secret are independently generated 32-byte CSPRNG values --
      asserted structurally, not inferred from them merely differing once.
- [ ] Changing the password requires the OLD password; a wrong one fails indistinguishably and
      changes nothing.
- [ ] After a successful change the config is 0600 (verified under umask 000) and the write is
      atomic; a simulated write failure leaves the OLD password still working and the verifier
      unchanged.
- [ ] The acting session still works after the change, and every other pre-change session is refused.
- [ ] After POST /logout, replaying the PRE-LOGOUT session cookie on an authenticated route is
      REFUSED. A logout that only clears the browser cookie while leaving the server entry live
      passes every other listed test.
- [ ] Session establishment is reachable from a verified principal without going through the
      password verifier, so a second credential type would touch only the verifier.
- [ ] The password change runs in ONE critical section spanning verify, write, verifier swap and
      session invalidation, proven by a concurrency test: two sessions changing the password at once
      must not leave disk holding one password and memory another.

title: daemon: ?status=open filter on /v1/history (the one 6c daemon change)
description:
Daemon: add a `?status=open` filter to GET /v1/history.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.4. The ONLY daemon change Phase 6c is permitted; ships
as its own PR against a daemon that is in production holding real funds.

Problem: LN payments can hold for hours or days (ADR-0024), but HistoryQuery accepts only `limit`
and `before_seq`, so "what is outstanding right now" is unanswerable and a days-old held payment is
effectively invisible.

Required:
1. `HistoryQuery` gains an optional `status`; `?status=open` returns exactly `Started`+`Awaiting`.
2. **Apply the filter INSIDE the journal scan, before `take(limit)`.** `journal.rs::history()`
   already filters `before_seq` inside the same iterator chain — put the status filter there.
   Filtering in the handler AFTER `history(limit, ..)` returns would filter an already-truncated
   page, so an open row behind `limit` newer terminal rows disappears — the exact failure this
   feature exists to prevent. This matches the CLI's documented "filters apply before limit".
3. Read-only: must not touch the actor, executor, or any money path.
4. Omitting `status` must be byte-identical to today's response; cursor paging must still work.
5. An unrecognised status value returns **422 `refused`** (the daemon's existing malformed-query
   contract), not 400 and never a silent unfiltered listing.
6. `history()` currently SKIPS UNDECODABLE ledger rows silently. On the status=open path that lets
   a corrupt open operation vanish while the UI says "nothing outstanding". Signal that rows were
   skipped so the caller can fail closed.

Tests: exact Started+Awaiting set; omitting status unchanged; **an open row older than MORE THAN
ONE FULL PAGE of terminal rows is still returned** (a handler-side filter must FAIL this test —
verify it does by trying that implementation); cursor paging with the filter on; unknown status →
422; skipped-row signalling.

Scope guard: no other endpoint, no SSE, no actor/executor/journal-schema/money-path changes. The
diff should be readable in one sitting.
7. PIN THE WIRE CONTRACT for the skipped-row signal rather than improvising it at implementation
   time: an OPTIONAL integer field (e.g. `skipped_rows`) on the history response, emitted ONLY when non-zero (keeping the response minimal), and never at all on the unfiltered
   path -- that second rule, not this one, is what preserves the unfiltered byte-identical
   guarantee; `status=open` is a new query with no prior baseline to match. It counts rows the scan
   could not decode WHOSE SEQ LIES IN THE SEQ SPAN THIS PAGE CONSUMED (so exhaustive paging sums
   without double-counting; a whole-scan count would re-report the same corrupt rows on every
   page), and it is emitted ONLY on the `status=open` path --
   never on an unfiltered request, which must stay byte-identical even over a corrupt store. This
   is the sole production-daemon API change and its shape is now pinned in plan §6c.4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ?status=open returns exactly the Started+Awaiting set and excludes Succeeded/Failed.
- [ ] Omitting status produces a byte-identical response to today's behaviour.
- [ ] An open row older than MORE THAN ONE FULL PAGE of terminal rows is still returned. A handler-side filter applied after history(limit,..) MUST fail this test: try that implementation first and confirm it goes red, otherwise the test proves nothing.
- [ ] Cursor paging via before_seq/next_before_seq still works with the filter applied.
- [ ] An unrecognised status value returns 422 refused, never 400 and never a silent unfiltered listing.
- [ ] Skipped undecodable ledger rows are signalled in the response so the caller can fail closed rather than render an empty list.
- [ ] The pre-existing daemon suite still passes and the diff touches no actor, executor, or money path.
- [ ] The skipped-row field is optional, absent when zero, and a corrupt-row fixture proves the
      end-to-end value while an uncorrupted response stays byte-identical to today's.

title: wallet-web: read surface (dashboard, Outstanding, activity, operation detail)
description:
`wallet-web` read surface: dashboard, Outstanding, activity, operation detail, federations.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.4, §6c.5. Depends on auth + the ?status=open filter.

Required:
1. Server-rendered HTML via `askama` (compile-time templates, no runtime loading, no bundler).
2. Pages: Dashboard (unified balance, per-federation breakdown, Outstanding, recent activity);
   Activity (paginated history via the existing before_seq/next_before_seq cursor); Operation
   detail; Federations list.
3. **Outstanding must follow `next_before_seq` TO EXHAUSTION**, bounded by a page cap. **If the cap
   is reached the list MUST be labelled incomplete in the UI** -- presenting a truncated list as the
   complete Outstanding set hides exactly the old held payment this feature exists to surface. Test
   the cap-hit state explicitly. One request
   returns at most `limit` rows, so rendering a single page and calling it "all outstanding" is a
   lie — the whole point is that an old held operation stays visible.
4. If the daemon signals that undecodable rows were skipped, render a **fail-closed warning**, not
   an empty/short list.
5. **Operation detail renders ONLY what `OperationView` carries** (kind, status, amount, fees,
   actor, reason, error, refusal). It does NOT show a Stranded move's preimage or leg op-ids: the
   wire DTO carries neither and the rich move record is `--standalone` only. A stranded operation
   renders its `error` string verbatim and links the runbook's stranded-move incident entry. Do NOT describe it as a 'stop-the-daemon
   recovery procedure': the runbook stops the daemon to PRESERVE EVIDENCE, because no shipped
   command can display the preimage, and the only stop-the-daemon restore in that document is the
   unrelated disk-loss path.
   (The earlier version of this bead required the preimage; that was unbuildable inside the
   one-daemon-change budget. Do not re-add it.)
6. The browser holds NO wallet state; every page reconstructs from the daemon. No CDN, no external
   fonts, no telemetry; assets compiled into the binary.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes): never "risk engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb,
"curated", or "anonymous". Amounts in sats with msat precision where non-zero. Agent/evacuation
actions money-centric, past-tense, with reasons.

Tests: pages rejected without a session; Outstanding lists exactly the non-terminal set AND pages to
exhaustion when there are more open operations than one page; history paging follows the cursor;
skipped-row warning renders.

Scope guard: read-only — no money forms, no admin forms, no JS yet. No framework, no htmx, no npm.
Never compute or re-derive a balance or fee in the frontend.
7. Outstanding renders each operation's AGE (the plan requires it), and the paging cap is
   CONCRETE: follow next_before_seq for at most 10 pages (500 rows at the default limit of 50) or
   5 seconds, whichever comes first. On hitting either bound, or on a mid-sequence page fetch
   FAILING, render the list explicitly labelled incomplete with the reason -- never silently
   truncated and never presented as the whole set.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dashboard, Activity, Operation detail and Federations render with a valid session and are rejected without one.
- [ ] Outstanding lists exactly the non-terminal set, and when there are MORE open operations than one page it follows next_before_seq to exhaustion rather than showing only the newest page.
- [ ] When the page cap is reached the list is labelled incomplete in the UI, with a test for that state. A truncated list presented as complete hides the old held payment this feature exists to surface.
- [ ] When the daemon signals skipped undecodable rows, a fail-closed warning renders instead of a short or empty list.
- [ ] Operation detail renders only fields OperationView actually carries. A Stranded move renders its error string verbatim and links the runbook's stranded-move INCIDENT entry (labelling that link a "recovery procedure" FAILS this criterion -- the runbook preserves evidence and offers no recovery flow); it does NOT claim to show a preimage or leg op-ids, which the wire DTO does not carry.
- [ ] History paging follows the existing cursor contract.
- [ ] No balance or fee is computed or re-derived in the frontend; every figure comes from the API.
- [ ] No asset is fetched from a third party at runtime.
- [ ] Each Outstanding row shows its age.
- [ ] With more open operations than the cap, the list renders labelled incomplete with the reason.
- [ ] When a page fetch fails midway, the partial list renders labelled incomplete rather than as a
      complete set or an error page.
- [ ] Activity exposes the ONE filter the plan defines -- outstanding versus all -- as a working
      control. Shipping Activity with no filter at all satisfies every other criterion here.

title: wallet-web: on-screen polling, degraded-daemon banner, /healthz
description:
`wallet-web`: on-screen polling, degraded-daemon banner, /healthz.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.4, §6c.6. Depends on the read surface.

Required:
1. ~50 lines of VANILLA JS compiled into the binary, doing two jobs only: polling on-screen
   operations, and disabling a submit button after click. No framework, no htmx, no bundler, no npm,
   no CDN. (Note: the button disable is a convenience — the real double-submit defence is
   render-time idempotency keys + PRG in br-t8f, because the UI must work without JS.)
2. Polling: GET /v1/operations/{key} every 3s for VISIBLE operations, stopping on terminal status
   and on `visibilitychange`. Polling is a live-view convenience, NOT the tracking mechanism —
   Outstanding is. Browsers throttle background timers and suspend mobile pages.
3. **Polling requests must be PASSIVE with respect to the session**: they must not slide
   `last_seen`, or an open tab stays authorized for the full 24h and the idle timeout never fires.
   (Enforced in br-nfz; do not defeat it here by routing polling through an activity-updating path.)
4. UI degrades honestly without JS: forms work, pages just do not live-update.
5. Daemon unreachable: READ PAGES render a clear banner. (The money/admin form-disable behaviour is
   specified in the plan but is NOT verified here: those forms are built by br-t8f and br-ucq, which
   this task does not depend on, so asserting them here would be impossible in the declared order.
   That integration check belongs to the final gate, br-4yz.)
6a. NOTE the asymmetry: a DOWN sidecar cannot answer at all, so sidecar-down is signalled to the
   supervisor by CONNECTION FAILURE, not by a field. /healthz answers only for a LIVE sidecar and
   reports {sidecar_alive: true, daemon_reachable: <bool>}. Do not claim the endpoint distinguishes
   both states by payload; it cannot.
6. `GET /healthz` is an explicit, deliberate exception to "every route requires a session" — a
   supervisor cannot log in. Restrict it to exactly two booleans (sidecar alive, daemon reachable).
   It MUST expose no balance, no operation, no federation, and no version detail, and it must be in
   the route-manifest allowlist so the carve-out is asserted rather than accidental.

Tests: polling stops at terminal status; continuous polling does not extend a session (covered in
br-nfz item 5 — do not regress it); degraded banner appears on read pages; /healthz
reports {sidecar_alive: true, daemon_reachable: <bool>} and leaks nothing else (sidecar-down is a
CONNECTION FAILURE, not a payload -- see item 6a).

Scope guard: no SSE, no WebSockets, no service worker, no notifications (ADR-0028 deferred all).
No second JS file, no build step.
7. OWN THE SHARED DEGRADED-STATE CONTRACT. Expose one reachability signal plus the form-marker
   convention (e.g. a template helper / CSS marker) that br-t8f and br-ucq apply to their own
   forms. Those beads render the disabled state; this bead defines the mechanism they call, so the
   behaviour has ONE implementation owner rather than being discovered missing at the final gate.
8. Define the SUBMIT-DISABLE contract too (the JS's second job): a documented form marker that
   br-t8f and br-ucq apply. This bead defines and unit-tests the mechanism; br-4yz verifies it
   against the real money and admin forms once they exist.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every user-facing string this bead renders --
including login, settings and error text: never "risk engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb,
"curated", or "anonymous".
The degraded-mode text is the sharpest case: it must say plainly that the wallet daemon is not
responding, not reassure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Polling updates a visible operation and stops on terminal status and on visibilitychange.
- [ ] Polling does NOT extend the session idle timer (the assertion lives in br-nfz; this bead must not defeat it by routing polling through an activity-updating path).
- [ ] Read pages render a clear banner when the daemon is unreachable. The money/admin form-disable check belongs to br-4yz, where those forms exist.
- [ ] /healthz distinguishes sidecar-alive from daemon-reachable and exposes NOTHING else: no balance, no operation, no federation, no version.
- [ ] The UI still functions with JavaScript disabled: forms submit, pages simply do not live-update.
- [ ] Total JavaScript stays under roughly 50 lines, with no framework, bundler, or npm dependency.
- [ ] The degraded-state contract is documented and callable by other surfaces, not private to
      this bead's read pages.
- [ ] The submit-disable marker is documented and exercised, not merely asserted to exist.
- [ ] The degraded-mode and health strings conform to the copy canon and state the real condition.
- [ ] The ACTUAL polling endpoint, hit continuously with a valid session, does not slide
      `last_seen`; likewise /healthz presented with a cookie. br-nfz can only test a synthetic
      passive route because the real one does not exist at its stage, so if this bead routes polling
      through an activity-updating path BOTH beads pass while the idle timeout is defeated.

title: wallet-web: money surface (send, receive+QR, move, direct-inflow)
description:
`wallet-web` money surface: send, receive with server-side QR, move, direct-inflow.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.3, §6c.5 (including "Idempotency and double-submit" and
"Money form contracts"). Depends on the read surface.

MONEY-CRITICAL. `ReceiveRequest.nonce` and `MoveRequest.occurrence` are CLIENT-SUPPLIED idempotency
inputs: a refresh or resubmit that regenerates them is admitted by the daemon as a SECOND money
operation. A JS button-disable is not a defence — the spec requires the UI to work without JS.

Required:
1. Every money form GENERATES ITS IDEMPOTENCY VALUE AT RENDER TIME into a hidden field, so a
   resubmit of the same rendered form carries the same key and dedupes at the daemon. Preserve it
   through preview/confirm/retry.
2. Pay and Move use Post/Redirect/Get so a refresh re-issues a GET. Receive and DirectInflow do
   NOT redirect -- their invoice exists only in the POST response body and a browser does not
   render a redirect's body, so they render the result in place. That is safe because the
   idempotency key is fixed at render time and the daemon re-yields the same invoice. Do NOT store
   transient result state in the sidecar to work around this.
2b. Snapshot policy-derived fields into the form. The idempotency value alone does NOT guarantee
   replay: when federation or fee cap are unset the daemon resolves them from CURRENT policy per
   POST, and for a move the resolved fee cap is an INPUT TO THE OPERATION KEY
   (handlers.rs: `let fee_cap = request.fee_cap.unwrap_or(policy.max_fee)` feeding `move_key`).
   A policy edit between the first POST and a retry then yields a different key from the same
   occurrence and admits a SECOND move. Each rendered form must submit EXPLICIT federation and
   fee-cap values.
3. Send: paste a BOLT11 invoice, show a decoded preview (amount, destination, expiry) BEFORE
   submit, allow a fee cap, confirm, POST /v1/pay.
4. Receive and DirectInflow return their payable invoice ONLY in the POST response. Redirecting
   straight to the operation page would discard it — render a RESULT PAGE carrying the invoice, its
   server-rendered QR, the operation key, and a link to the detail page. Re-attaching the same
   receive key re-yields the same invoice, which also fixes refresh-loses-the-invoice.
5. QR rendered SERVER-SIDE as inline SVG (`qrcode` crate). No JS QR library, no external service.
6. Move (/v1/move) and DirectInflow (/v1/direct-inflow) forms.
7. Per-form contract: which federation (selector where the DTO accepts one, defaulted to the policy
   spending pin), which fields are optional, and units. **Amounts are exact decimal sats with at
   most three fractional digits, converted to integer msat WITHOUT floating point.** Never parse an
   amount into f64.
8. Operations here are `Actor::User` — no Actor enum change.
9. Pay is async and may settle hours later (ADR-0024). The UI must never imply settlement because
   the POST returned 2xx.

Tests: malformed invoice rejected before submit; decoded preview matches the invoice; QR payload
equals the invoice string; **submitting the same rendered receive/move form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT
DISABLED produces exactly ONE operation -- and the Move case MUST edit `max_fee` between the two
submissions and still yield ONE operation**, since a test that does not touch policy passes even
when the form omits the cap and lets the daemon re-derive it into a different `move_key` (which is
the whole defect); likewise assert Receive keeps its snapshotted federation and cap across a policy
edit; the same receive key re-yields the same invoice; result page carries invoice+QR.

Scope guard: no LNURL, no Lightning Address, no on-chain, no amountless invoices. No retry, fallback
or route logic in the frontend — the engine owns that. Never re-sum fees client-side.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every string this bead renders: never use "risk
engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb, "curated", or "anonymous". Amounts display in sats with
msat precision where non-zero. Agent and evacuation actions are described money-centric,
past-tense, with reasons.
10. RENDER MONEY FORMS DISABLED when the daemon is unreachable, using br-pfc's shared
    degraded-state contract, with an explanation rather than failing on submit. br-4yz verifies
    this end to end; the implementation is owned HERE.
11. DirectInflow carries its OWN client nonce (`DirectInflowRequest.nonce`, wallet-api/src/lib.rs:271),
    so it is subject to the identical render-time idempotency rule as Receive. Do not treat it as a
    lesser sibling of the receive flow.
12. THE TEST DAEMON MUST USE THE REAL KEY DERIVATION. "Exactly ONE operation" and "the same
    receive key re-yields the same invoice" are DAEMON-side behaviours, and a real invoice needs a
    live federation, so these tests necessarily run against a fake daemon. That fake MUST compute
    admission keys by calling the actual functions -- `move_key`, `direct_inflow_nonce_key`,
    `raw_receive_key` (all `pub` in `wallet-fedimint`, already imported at handlers.rs:29) -- and
    For POLICY RESOLUTION the real function is NOT importable -- `resolve_fed` is a private fn in
    `wallet-daemon`, which is a binary-only crate with no lib.rs -- so the fake must instead
    replicate the two-line rule EXPLICITLY and cite it: fee_cap = request.fee_cap OR
    policy.max_fee; to = request.to OR policy.spending_fed (handlers.rs:335-336, :305/:374/:398).
    Do not refactor the daemon to expose it: that would breach the one-daemon-change budget.
    A natural fake that dedupes on `occurrence`/`nonce` alone NULLIFIES the whole suite: the
    max_fee-edit test then passes against exactly the broken form it exists to catch, because the
    fake never feeds the cap into the key. This is the single highest user-visible risk of the
    phase, and the test's apparent rigor would otherwise manufacture false confidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A malformed invoice is rejected before submission, and the decoded preview (amount, destination, expiry) matches the invoice.
- [ ] Receive renders a server-side SVG QR whose payload equals the invoice string exactly.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered receive form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly ONE operation and the same invoice.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered move form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly ONE operation EVEN WHEN max_fee IS EDITED BETWEEN THE TWO SUBMISSIONS. A test that does not change policy between submissions passes against the broken implementation too and therefore proves nothing.
- [ ] Receive keeps its snapshotted federation and fee cap across a policy edit.
- [ ] Pay and Move redirect after POST; Receive and DirectInflow render their result in place, because the invoice exists only in the POST body. No transient result state is stored in the sidecar.
- [ ] Amounts are parsed as exact decimal sats to integer msat with no floating point anywhere in the path.
- [ ] The UI never implies a payment settled merely because the POST returned 2xx.
- [ ] Every user-facing string this bead adds conforms to the copy canon.
- [ ] Submitting the same rendered DIRECTINFLOW form twice WITH JAVASCRIPT DISABLED yields exactly
      ONE operation and the same invoice, and its result page carries the invoice, QR, operation key
      and detail link. Testing only Receive and Move leaves this duplicate-money path unproven.
- [ ] Amount conversion is proven by a boundary table, not a token case: 1 sat; 1.001 sat; 0.001 sat;
      more than three fractional digits REJECTED; malformed input REJECTED; a value large enough to
      overflow REJECTED. Each accepted case yields the exact integer msat with no floating point
      anywhere in the path, so a 1000x units error cannot pass.
- [ ] Money forms render disabled (not failing-on-submit) when the daemon is unreachable.
- [ ] DirectInflow replay under POLICY MUTATION: render once, submit, then change BOTH the spending
      pin and max_fee, resubmit the identical rendered form with JS disabled, and assert ONE
      operation, the same invoice, and the ORIGINAL destination and cap. `DirectInflowRequest.to` is
      Option and the handler resolves policy.spending_fed before keying (handlers.rs:391), so a form
      omitting it passes an unchanged-policy test and duplicates after a pin change.
- [ ] Pay's rendered request also carries explicit federation and fee cap: the snapshot rule is for
      EVERY money form, not only those with an obvious nonce.
- [ ] Log capture over a SUCCESSFUL and a FAILING daemon call proves no full invoice and no bearer
      token is emitted at any level; a static grep misses structured logging of a request object.
- [ ] The test daemon calls the real `move_key` / `direct_inflow_nonce_key` / `raw_receive_key`;
      re-implementing THOSE is a defect. Policy resolution is the stated exception -- `resolve_fed`
      is private to a binary-only crate, so requirement 12's explicit two-line replica IS the
      mandated approach there, not a shortcut.
- [ ] Prove the harness is not vacuous: with the FORM deliberately broken (omitting the fee cap so
      the daemon re-derives it), the max_fee-edit test must FAIL. A suite that stays green against
      that form is testing nothing.
- [ ] The fake ALSO models live-attach sizing validation, not only key derivation: `raw_receive_key`
      omits the fee cap while `validate_live_attach` COMPARES it (wallet-fedimint/src/service/actor.rs
      ~2140-2173). A fake deduping on the key alone re-yields the invoice and passes the
      policy-mutation test while the real walletd returns a sizing conflict. Prove non-vacuity: the
      deliberately-broken form must make this test FAIL.

title: wallet-web: federation, admin, policy, diagnostics surfaces
description:
`wallet-web` federation, admin, policy, and diagnostics surfaces.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.3, §6c.5. Depends on the read surface.

Required:
1. Federations: join (/v1/join), candidates (/v1/candidates), approve (/v1/approve).
2. Admin: reconcile (/v1/reconcile), recover (/v1/recover).
3. **Diagnostics panel** surfacing /v1/status, /v1/watch/status and /v1/health (scheduler alive,
   watch state, daemon health). These are part of the "full parity" claim and previously had no
   page and no bead — that was a coverage gap.
4. Policy view + edit. **Read-modify-write, never reconstruct**: `PUT /v1/policy` takes a WHOLE
   `Policy`, and new policy fields ship `#[serde(default)]`, so a form that rebuilds `Policy` from
   only the fields it knows would SILENTLY RESET any field added later — including money caps. GET
   the current policy, merge the edited fields into that value, PUT the result.
5. Policy edits state units explicitly (msat vs bps). The runbook's cap arithmetic was previously
   wrong precisely because units were ambiguous.
6. Every destructive/irreversible action — recover, approve, join, policy edits — requires an
   explicit CONFIRMATION STEP on a separate page naming in plain language what will happen.
   `recover` re-seeds a wallet; `approve` decides which federations become fundable (the trust
   decision ADR-0017's probe gate protects). This is a UI affordance, NOT an auth gate: ADR-0028
   chose no step-up and this must not smuggle one back in.
7. The seed/mnemonic is NEVER exposed by any route to any session. Seed export stays CLI-only and
   daemon-stopped (runbook Day 0).

Tests: each destructive action requires passing its confirmation page; **a policy round-trip
preserves a field the form does not know about** (prove read-modify-write, not reconstruct); no
route returns seed material; diagnostics render.

Scope guard: no multi-user, no roles, no new daemon endpoints. No policy validation logic in the
frontend — submit and render what the daemon says.

Copy canon (roadmap-to-v1.md 6b notes) applies to every string this bead renders: never use "risk
engine", "safe", "bank", "mint" as a verb, "curated", or "anonymous". Amounts display in sats with
msat precision where non-zero. Agent and evacuation actions are described money-centric,
past-tense, with reasons.
This matters most on the confirmation pages, which must name the real consequence in plain language
rather than reassuring the user.
8. RENDER ADMIN AND POLICY FORMS DISABLED when the daemon is unreachable, using br-pfc's shared
   degraded-state contract, with an explanation rather than failing on submit.
9. STATE THE CONFIRMATION CONTRACT MECHANICALLY. It is a UI affordance, NOT an auth gate

   ONLY on its confirmation page, which names the consequence in plain language. The test asserts
   the two-step flow and the page's content. It must NOT assert that a direct POST carrying valid
   CSRF is rejected -- that would be the step-up gate the ADR excluded, and testing it as a
   rejection would silently reintroduce one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Join, approve, candidates, reconcile, recover and policy view/edit are reachable and function against the daemon.
- [ ] Every destructive or irreversible action (recover, approve, join, policy edit) requires passing an explicit confirmation page that names the consequence in plain language.
- [ ] A policy edit preserves a field the form does not know about, proving read-modify-write rather than reconstruct. Rebuilding Policy from known fields would silently reset serde-default fields including money caps.
- [ ] Policy units are stated explicitly (msat vs bps) on every editable field.
- [ ] The diagnostics panel surfaces /v1/status, /v1/watch/status and /v1/health.
- [ ] No route returns seed or mnemonic material under any circumstance.
- [ ] Every user-facing string this bead adds conforms to the copy canon, and each confirmation
      page names the actual consequence rather than reassuring.
- [ ] Admin and policy forms render disabled (not failing-on-submit) when the daemon is unreachable.
- [ ] The two-step flow and confirmation-page content are asserted; a direct POST with valid CSRF
      is NOT asserted to fail (that would be a step-up gate ADR-0028 excluded).

description:
`wallet-web` live devimint gate + the final route manifest test.

Spec: docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md §6c.7. Depends on all other 6c beads.

Two deliverables:

**A. The final route manifest test** (belongs here, after all routes exist — not in the auth bead,
where most routes did not yet exist):
- Enumerate EVERY route. Each must either require a session or appear on the explicit allowlist
  (`GET /login`, `POST /login`, `GET /healthz`). A newly added route fails by default.
- Assert the required security headers on EVERY response class: authenticated pages, redirects,
  errors, the login page, and /healthz.

**B. The live gate**, driven like the existing CLI devimint gates (wallet-cli/tests/smoke_*.sh),
against a two-fed devimint with walletd + wallet-web running:
1. Log in over HTTP with the configured password.
2. Receive: create an invoice through the UI, pay it externally, see settlement appear.
3. Send: pay an invoice and see the operation terminalize.
4. Long-running tracking: an in-flight operation appears under Outstanding, then RESTART THE
   BROWSER SESSION (new client, no cookies or state) and confirm it is still listed with correct
   status — proving the UI holds no client state and the journal is the truth.
5. Kill walletd: degraded banner appears AND the money and admin forms are disabled with an
   explanation rather than failing on submit. This cross-surface check lives here, not in br-pfc:
   the forms are built by br-t8f and br-ucq, so this is the first point where every piece exists.
   Restart walletd and confirm recovery.

Run everything inside `nix develop /home/master/p/fedimint -c ...` — bare cargo fails on missing
cmake. Use release binaries and REBUILD them before the run; a stale binary silently invalidates the
gate (this has bitten this project twice).

Capture the REAL exit code into the log (write REAL_GATE_EXIT=$? and grep it) — the trailing
command's exit status is not the gate's.

Scope guard: this bead writes AND RUNS the gate. A gate that is only reviewed and never executed is
worthless, and a false PASS is worse than no gate. Before declaring green, make one assertion fail
deliberately and confirm the gate goes red.
C. OWN THE FINAL DEFINITION OF DONE. Before declaring the phase complete, assert on the final
   tree: the default `cargo test` suite passes; `cargo fmt --check` is clean; `cargo clippy
   -D warnings` is clean; NO JavaScript toolchain, bundler, or npm dependency was introduced; the
   daemon diff is limited to the `?status=open` filter and its tests; no runtime dependency fetches
   a third-party asset; and the crate is within the plan's ~2,000-3,000 line budget (report the
   number, and if materially over, say what grew rather than quietly passing).
D. The final manifest must ALSO classify and exercise CSRF/ORIGIN on EVERY mutating route. br-nfz
   can only cover routes existing during auth work, so money, recovery, approval, join, policy,
   logout and password routes could bypass the middleware entirely while both beads still pass. For
   each POST/PUT: reject with no CSRF token, with a mismatched Origin, and with neither Origin nor
   Referer -- all BEFORE handler execution. POST /login is the sole token exception and must still
   fail its origin checks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The final route manifest test enumerates EVERY route; each either requires a session or appears on the explicit allowlist (GET /login, POST /login, GET /healthz). A newly added route fails this test by default.
- [ ] Required security headers are asserted on every response class: authenticated pages, redirects, errors, login, and /healthz.
- [ ] Live on devimint: log in, create an invoice through the UI, have it paid externally, and observe settlement.
- [ ] Live: pay an invoice and watch the operation terminalize.
- [ ] Live: an in-flight operation appears under Outstanding, SURVIVES A BROWSER RESTART with no cookies or client state, and is still listed with correct status.
- [ ] Live: killing walletd produces the degraded banner AND disables money and admin forms with an explanation rather than failing on submit; restarting recovers.
- [ ] The gate is RUN, not merely written: before declaring green, break one assertion deliberately and confirm the gate goes red.
- [ ] The real exit code is captured in the log (REAL_GATE_EXIT) rather than inferred from a trailing command.
- [ ] A repository-wide assertion proves NO route returns seed or mnemonic material: enumerate every
      route, exercise it with a valid session, and assert no response body contains the mnemonic.
      This is a global invariant, so it is asserted once here rather than per-surface.
- [ ] A single global string audit confirms no user-facing text anywhere violates the copy canon.
- [ ] Final DoD asserted on the finished tree: cargo test, fmt, clippy -D warnings, no JS toolchain,
      daemon diff limited to the one change, no third-party runtime asset, line budget reported.
- [ ] The restarted browser in the Outstanding check LOGS IN AGAIN before inspecting state -- a
      cookie-free client cannot read anything under the auth contract, so the step is otherwise
      impossible as written.
- [ ] Every mutating route is enumerated and proven to reject a missing CSRF token and a bad Origin
      before the handler runs; POST /login is exempt from the token only, never from the origin check.
- [ ] The promised repository-wide log audit is performed: no password, session token, bearer token,
      or full invoice appears in any log statement.
- [ ] The Outstanding survival check restarts `wallet-web` TOO, not just the browser -- restarting the
      browser alone would pass a sidecar serving stale in-memory state, which is the very premise
      under test.
- [ ] COLD START degraded mode: start `wallet-web` with `walletd` absent, assert /healthz reports the
      daemon unreachable and authenticated pages show the banner, then start `walletd` and confirm
      recovery. Killing an already-connected daemon would pass an implementation that refuses to boot
      without one.
- [ ] The security-header assertion runs over EVERY registered route, not one example per response
      class. A later money or recovery route can bypass the header layer while login, one redirect,
      one error and /healthz keep a class-based test green. Keep the representative redirect/error
      cases in addition to per-route coverage.
- [ ] The live gate includes ONE JS-disabled double-submit replay against the REAL daemon (submit a
      rendered money form twice) and asserts a single operation. The unit suite necessarily uses a
      fake daemon, so without this the duplicate-payment defence is never exercised end to end.

title: Correct what Stranded means: not a gateway failure, and the preimage does not recover it
description:
Correct what `Stranded` is documented to mean, in code, ledger text, tests, and the runbook.

## Why this is P1

Not because anything behaves wrongly -- nothing does -- but because the wrong description actively
misleads, and has already demonstrably done so. During the 2026-08-01 analysis it led to a proposal
to build preimage-recovery tooling that could not have recovered anything, caught only because
someone asked why it was needed. A wrong explanation of a money state reproduces itself faster than
it gets checked: the exact stale phrases now appear at 17 sites across 9 tracked files.

## What this bead asserts -- and deliberately does NOT

Three independent adversarial audits of the FIRST drafts of this bead each found a false protocol
claim in the causal story it tried to tell (that forfeit can never strand; that a receive `Failure`
proves the contract was claimed; that a same-seed clone alone can steal the claim). The state has
NEVER been observed in production. That track record is itself the finding: an exhaustive causal
taxonomy of an unobserved state does not survive contact with the protocol, and a code comment is
the worst place to keep one.

So this bead corrects the FALSE claims and stops there. It does NOT establish a complete cause
list. Anything it says about causes is explicitly a non-exhaustive operator aid living in the
runbook, not an invariant in a doc comment.

**What is solidly established (survived all three audits, verified at the pin `72b1e5be`,
wallet-fedimint/Cargo.toml:20):**

- **A misbehaving gateway alone cannot strand a move.** A's send reaches `Success` only against a
  preimage verified against the outgoing contract (`lnv2-client/send_sm.rs:208-211`,
  `lnv2-common/contracts.rs:186-191`), or via A's guardians' `await_preimage`, populated only on a
  verified claim (`lnv2-server/lib.rs:465-476`). B's preimage is derived CLIENT-side as
  `sha256(sha256(ECDH-tweak))` (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:881-889`) and never transmitted; the only copy
  leaving the client is threshold-encrypted to B's guardians (`lnv2-common/contracts.rs:84-89`).
  The gateway holds ciphertext it cannot open.
- **The preimage is NOT the recovery instrument.** It claims A's OUTGOING contract, and a
  send-`Success` means that contract has already been claimed or is claimable by the party holding
  the preimage; spending it is additionally authorised to `claim_pk` (`lnv2-server/lib.rs:465-476`),
  not by the preimage alone. Nothing about it credits B. Where recovery is possible at all the
  instrument is B's claim material (`contract`, `claim_keypair`, `agg_decryption_key`), which the
  SDK persists in `ReceiveSMCommon` (`lnv2-client/receive_sm.rs:35-40`).
- **Forfeit NORMALLY refunds, but "never strands" is FALSE.** The gateway's cancel signature drives
  an immediate refund (`lnv2-client/send_sm.rs:238-266`, `lnv2-server/lib.rs:485-491`) -> normally
  `MovePhase::Refunded`. BUT if the gateway incorrectly claimed the outgoing contract and the refund
  transaction is therefore rejected, the SDK re-checks `await_preimage` and PROMOTES the leg to
  send-`Success` (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:705-725`). That send-Success can then meet a non-claimed
  receive and land in `Stranded`. Document the normal outcome AND this race; do not write "never".
- **A receive `Failure` proves very little.** It is yielded whenever `await_primary_module_outputs`
  fails (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:1049-1053`), which collapses two structurally different mint states
  (`mint-client/src/output.rs:53-71`, `mint-client/src/lib.rs:1528-1534`): `Aborted` (the containing
  transaction was REJECTED -- nothing claimed) and `Failed` (accepted, then issuance failed). It
  therefore does NOT prove the contract was claimed, does NOT prove funds reached B's mint, and
  does NOT exclude a malicious federation -- `output.rs:68-71` says `Failed` "should never happen
  with a honest federation and bug-free code". The honest operator statement is
  **"not proven lost, and not proven recoverable"**, with the uncertainty stated.
- **A second claimant needs more than the seed.** lnv2 has `type Backup = NoModuleBackup`
  (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:329`) and starts a receive SM only when given the specific randomized
  contract (`:964-994`), so a seed-only recovery does NOT resume an in-flight receive. Another
  claimant requires duplicated in-flight client state (a copied data directory, a second daemon on
  the same disk) or explicit access to the contract and claim material. This remains worth checking
  first because it is cheap to rule out and severe if true -- but it is a HYPOTHESIS, not a
  measurement, and "same seed" alone is not sufficient to cause it. Note also that a prior claimant
  is one route INTO the rejected-transaction/`Aborted` class above, not a separate parallel cause;
  do not present them as independent.

## Required changes

1. `wallet-fedimint/src/move_protocol.rs:21-26`: rewrite the `Stranded` doc comment. Keep it
   CONCISE and invariant-shaped -- what observation produces `Stranded` (send settled, receive
   terminal non-claim), what CANNOT be inferred from it (not a gateway fault; not proof of loss;
   not proof of malice), that the preimage does not recover it, and a pointer to the runbook as the
   canonical operator account. Do NOT embed a cause list here: that is the drift-prone thing this
   bead exists to remove.
2. `wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs:2020-2029` (`stranded_outcome` and its doc comment): the
   message ends "payment preimage saved on the move record" and the comment calls the preimage "the
   durable recovery artifact". Both send an operator after an artifact that cannot help.
   **HARD CONSTRAINT: the leading substring "send settled but receive was not credited" is the
   anchor the runbook's daily stranded check greps for** (docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:121).
   Either keep that substring byte-identical or update the runbook grep in the SAME change.
3. `wallet-fedimint/src/executor.rs:1564`: the inline "(the misbehaving-gateway T4 case)" comment.
4. Tests that assert the stale wording -- these are string-expectation updates, not behaviour
   changes: `executor.rs:3105`, `:3113` (the fabricated `"forfeited"` input at `:3109`), `:3123`,
   `:3157`, and the byte-for-byte ledger fixture at `wallet-fedimint/tests/probe_runtime.rs:708`.
   Replace the fabricated input with the only receive-failure string this wallet can produce, minted
   at `multi_client.rs:1429-1431`. (`"forfeited"` is not entirely absent from the pin -- it occurs
   once in a test doc comment, `lnv2-tests/bin/tests.rs:426` -- but no code path produces it as a
   receive-failure string.)
5. `wallet-fedimint/src/multi_client.rs:1429-1431`: the only receive-failure string the wallet can
   produce copies the SDK's understated "programming error or malicious federation" wording and
   omits the mint-leg cases entirely.
6. `docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md:162-179` (stranded incident entry): preserving the data
   directory is still right; the REASON and the next step are wrong. This entry becomes the
   canonical operator account: what cannot be inferred, "not proven lost / not proven recoverable",
   and "check whether another wallet instance is or was running against this data directory" as the
   FIRST diagnostic -- framed as cheapest-to-rule-out, not as the established cause.
7. Live docs that repeat the claim: `docs/phase4-implementation-spec.md:119, 131, 138, 148, 668`
   (authoritative -- `operation-history-spec.md` says the impl spec wins), `docs/roadmap-to-v1.md:78`,
   `docs/phase6c-web-frontend-plan.md:234-238`,
   `docs/adr/0028-web-frontend-localhost-sidecar-session-auth.md:89-93`, and bead `br-5om`.
8. Do NOT edit `docs/archive/**`. Those are historical snapshots of what was believed at the time
   (`integration-phase-plan.md:111`, `phase1-implementation-spec.md:380,389`,
   `2026-07-05-fresh-eyes-review.md:289`); rewriting them falsifies the record.

## Tests

- The corrected stranded tests (`settle_after_send_strands_on_terminal_non_claim`, executor.rs:3095,
  and `successful_send_then_terminal_failed_receive_strands_with_preimage`, executor.rs:3118 --
  note the latter's NAME also encodes the stale framing) use a receive-failure string the SDK can
  actually produce, and still map to `Stranded`.
- A test pins the ledger anchor substring the runbook greps for, so a future reword cannot silently
  break the daily check. Name the runbook in the test's comment.
- Behaviour is unchanged: no state-machine edit, no phase-set edit, no change to when `Stranded` is
  entered. Only descriptions, one fabricated test input, and the expectation strings that quote it.

## Scope guard

Do NOT change the state machine, the phase set, or when `Stranded` is entered. Do NOT build
preimage-extraction or recovery tooling: the preimage cannot recover a stranded move. Do NOT remove
the `Stranded` phase; it remains correct defensive modelling. Do NOT re-introduce an exhaustive
cause list into a code comment. Greenfield repo: no compatibility shims.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] MECHANICAL: `git grep -n -e "misbehaving-gateway" -e "payment proof saved" -e "preimage saved"
      -e "durable recovery artifact" -- '*.rs' 'docs/**' ':!docs/archive'` returns ZERO hits.
      (Scoped deliberately: `.beads/` is excluded because this bead's own text quotes the phrases,
      and `docs/archive/**` is excluded per required change 8.)
- [ ] The `Stranded` doc comment states the invariant and points to the runbook, and contains no
      enumerated cause list.
- [ ] No code comment, ledger string, live doc, ADR, or bead describes `Stranded` as caused by a
      misbehaving gateway, or the preimage as its recovery artifact.
- [ ] The runbook entry says "not proven lost, not proven recoverable", gives the duplicated-client
      check as the FIRST diagnostic framed as cheapest-to-rule-out, and does not claim the seed
      alone enables a second claimant.
- [ ] The forfeit path is documented as NORMALLY `Refunded`, with the claim/refund race
      (`lnv2-client/lib.rs:705-725`) that can promote it to send-`Success` named explicitly. An
      assertion that forfeit can never strand FAILS this criterion.
- [ ] The daily stranded check still fires: the ledger anchor substring is either unchanged or the
      runbook grep was updated in the same change, and a test pins whichever was chosen.
- [ ] No test asserts a receive-failure string that cannot occur; `"forfeited"` appears in no
      assertion.
- [ ] `cargo test` passes inside `nix develop` and behaviour is unchanged: no state-machine edit,
      no new money path.

title: Evacuate: base + proportional fee cap (absolute cap cannot fund a real evacuation)
description:
Give `Evacuate` a base + proportional fee cap so a full-balance evacuation is not refused on price.

Authority: [ADR-0029](docs/adr/0029-evacuation-must-be-executable.md). Amends
[ADR-0018](docs/adr/0018-v1-evacuation-balance-cap.md), whose balance cap still stands.

## The problem

`wallet-core/src/allocator.rs` builds the `Evacuate` action with `fee_cap: snapshot.max_fee` — the
single ABSOLUTE cap — immediately beneath a comment stating "Route economics NEVER gates an
evacuation -- a dying federation must be drained even when the route prices badly". The parameter
contradicts the intent it sits under.

At the runbook's suggested settings, with fees measured on the pilot gateway:
- per-federation cap 75,000,000 msat
- measured swap cost at 1,000,000 msat: send 8,948 + receive 8,900 = 17,848 (1.78%)
- the same rate on a full federation: ~1,338,600 msat
- `--max-fee` absolute cap: 50,000 msat
- **over cap by ~27x**, and the consequence depends on the gateway's FEE SHAPE. Two distinct
  failure modes, both real, established by reading `size_fresh_evacuation` (executor.rs:606-667),
  the fit predicate (executor.rs:814-829) and `total_within_cap` (fee.rs:160-164) -- which sums
  BOTH legs' quotes, each INCLUDING the gateway's base fee, against the cap:
  1. BASE FEES BELOW THE CAP -> CHUNK-DRAIN. A smaller net fits, so the evacuation is silently
     downsized (warning at :654-663). The occurrence advances every watch cycle
     (scheduler.rs:692-697) and `idem_evac` embeds it (allocator.rs:629), so a fresh Evacuate is
     emitted for the remainder and the balance drains in ~27 chunks at ~the same total fee. This
     is what the pilot's MEASURED gateway does.
  2. BASE FEES AT OR ABOVE THE CAP -> GENUINE REFUSAL. A base does not shrink with the amount, so
     if the two bases alone exceed fee_cap, NO candidate ever fits and the executor returns
     `Retryable` (:646-653) every tick -- a silent livelock, not a terminal failure. A gateway may
     charge bases summing to ~150 sats against the runbook's 50-sat cap, so this is reachable.
  An earlier draft of this bead claimed (1) is the only behaviour and refusal is impossible. That
  was wrong; do not reintroduce it. The fix addresses both: one operation instead of ~27, a faster
  exit from a dying federation, and no silent livelock when a gateway's base is high.

No evacuation has ever run in production, so this has never been observed. `Move` is unaffected:
it already uses a proportional cap (`move_fee_cap(amount, snapshot.max_fee_bps_of_move)`).

A flat percentage would fail at the opposite end. The gateway's INTENDED envelope is `SEND_FEE_LIMIT` (100 sats + 1.5%) plus
`RECEIVE_FEE_LIMIT` (50 sats + 0.5%) ~= 150 sats + 2%. Do NOT call this a protocol bound: at our
pinned SDK rev it is not enforced, because `PaymentFee` derives a lexicographic `PartialOrd` over
(base, parts_per_million) and the check is a single `.le(...)`, so a small base with an arbitrarily
large ppm passes (the upstream defect this project reported separately). Nor does it bound the
wallet's total cost, which also includes federation and mint-note fees. OUR cap is the only real
bound, which is exactly why its shape matters. Treat 200+3% as a pilot starting point; the base component
dominates at small amounts, so a legitimate worst case is 2.2% of a 75,000-sat evacuation but 17%
of a 1,000-sat one. Hence base + proportional.

## Required changes

1. Add an evacuation fee cap of the form `base + proportional`, defaulting to **200 sats + 3%**
   (covers the ~150 sats + 2% protocol worst case with headroom at every size). Both components
   configurable through `Policy` alongside the existing knobs, in msat and bps respectively.
2. `Evacuate`'s `fee_cap` is computed from that, NOT from `snapshot.max_fee`. Leave `Move` on
   `move_fee_cap(...)` untouched.
2b. The cap must bound the FINAL EXECUTED net, not the planned amount, AND survive replay.
   Today `fee_cap` is a single collapsed `Msat` on `Action::Evacuate`, `MovePlan`, `MoveParams` and
   `MoveRecord` (wallet-core/src/types.rs:490, move_protocol.rs:80, :98), so the executor cannot
   recompute base + bps x executed from it -- the (base, bps) COMPONENTS must travel to wherever
   the recompute happens, and this bead must decide where (on the Action, on the record, or
   re-derived from a plumbed Policy) and name the type changes that implies.
   Crash safety is the money-critical half: replay reconstructs `MoveParams.fee_cap` from the
   original plan (executor.rs:264) and `assemble_move_record` treats params as authoritative,
   overwriting the cached `fee_cap` (move_protocol.rs:297, :418), while `MoveMeta` persists the
   downsized AMOUNT but not its cap (move_protocol.rs:187). So after a receive commit plus cache
   loss, replay can restore the PLANNED-amount cap and authorise an excessive fee on the smaller
   executed net. Define a durable authority for the final cap and make reassembly honour it.
   The underlying hazard: The allocator fixes
   `Action::Evacuate.fee_cap` before execution (allocator.rs:558-626) while the executor may
   still clamp to a smaller net (executor.rs:629-665, 715-769) without recomputing it. A
   compliant-looking implementation could plan 75,000 sats, keep the matching cap, get clamped to
   1,000 sats, and permit a fee far above base + 3% of what actually moved. Recompute (or
   re-verify) the cap against the executed amount and persist the result.
3. `Policy` gains the new fields with `#[serde(default)]` so an existing stored policy still
   decodes and adopts the shipped defaults (the one forward-compat allowance this repo grants).
3b. Adding two `Policy` fields touches more than the allocator. Name and update every propagation
   surface: `wallet-api/src/lib.rs`, `wallet-fedimint/src/tick.rs`,
   `wallet-fedimint/src/service/mod.rs`, both CLI flag sets and their override paths
   (`wallet-cli/src/main.rs`), and `AllocatorSnapshot` (`wallet-core/src/types.rs:80`). Also
   correct `allocator.rs:598-604`, whose diagnostics comments and `max_fee_bps: None` recording
   ("Evacuation sizes off the ABSOLUTE max_fee, not the proportional bps") become false.
4. Update `docs/adr/0029-evacuation-must-be-executable.md` (this bead's authority doc) if
   implementation invalidates anything in it, `README.md` (the policy-knob section) AND
   `docs/real-sats-pilot-runbook.md` §4 so the suggested `policy set` includes the new
   knobs, and state plainly that the absolute `--max-fee` no longer bounds an evacuation.

## Tests

- A full-balance evacuation at the per-federation cap is ADMITTED at measured rates -- construct
  the case that is refused today and assert it now passes. This is the regression the bead exists
  for; a test that only exercises a small evacuation would pass before and after.
- A small evacuation (~1,000 sats) whose legitimate fee is a large PERCENTAGE of the amount is
  admitted, proving the base component works. A percentage-only cap must FAIL this test -- try it
  and confirm it goes red, so the test is not vacuous.
- A fee above base + proportional is still REFUSED: the cap must bound a hostile gateway, not
  merely stop refusing.
- Existing `Move` cap behaviour is unchanged, asserted explicitly.
- A stored policy written before this change still decodes and picks up the defaults.

## Scope guard

Do NOT change the per-federation balance cap (ADR-0018 stands), the evacuation trigger, or the
route. Do NOT remove the absolute `max_fee`: `Move` and the manual verbs still use it. Do NOT make
evacuation uncapped. Greenfield: the `#[serde(default)]` allowance above is the only compatibility
concession.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CLAMP SAFETY (the 2b criterion; money-critical, currently the easiest hole to ship): a test
      plans an evacuation at a large amount, forces the executor to clamp it to a much smaller net,
      and asserts the permitted fee is base + bps of the EXECUTED amount -- not of the planned one.
      Without this AC an implementation can pass every other criterion here and still authorise a
      75,000-sat-sized cap against a 1,000-sat move.
- [ ] CRASH SAFETY: a killpoint test drops the `MoveRecord` cache after the receive commit and
      asserts reassembly restores the final (clamped) cap, never the planned-amount cap.
- [ ] A gateway whose base fees exceed the cap no longer produces an indefinite `Retryable`
      livelock: assert the base+proportional cap admits it, and assert the OLD absolute cap
      refused it (this half IS assertable -- unlike full-size admission, refusal is real here).
- [ ] A full-balance evacuation at the per-federation cap is admitted AT FULL SIZE IN ONE
      operation. Assert against `max_affordable_evacuation_net`: the same case today is sized down
      to roughly 1/27th of the ask. Do NOT write this as "refused before the change" -- it is not
      refused, and a test asserting refusal cannot be constructed.
- [ ] A small evacuation whose legitimate fee is a large percentage of the amount is admitted, and
      a percentage-only cap is shown to fail that test.
- [ ] A fee exceeding base + proportional is still refused.
- [ ] `Move`'s cap behaviour is unchanged, asserted by test.

- [ ] The runbook's suggested policy includes the new knobs and states that `--max-fee` no longer
