title: Evacuate: fall back to a two-gateway Lightning hop when no gateway serves both feds
description:
Give `Evacuate` a second route: a real Lightning hop when no gateway serves both federations.

Authority: [ADR-0029](docs/adr/0029-evacuation-must-be-executable.md).
DEPENDS ON the evacuation fee-cap bead for INTERFACE SEQUENCING (both touch how an evacuation's
cap is computed and persisted). Note the earlier rationale was wrong: the absolute cap does not
refuse a hop evacuation either -- it would chunk-drain and be perfectly observable.

## The problem

Every cross-federation transfer resolves ONE gateway that serves both ends.
`resolve_move_gateway` and `resolve_fallback_move_gateway` both return a single `GatewayUrl` gated
on `gateway_serves_route(to, from)`; the so-called fallback resolver only searches for a CHEAPER
gateway that still serves both. NOTE the correct shape: `MovePlan` is explicitly GATEWAY-FREE (move_protocol.rs:85-102). The
single gateway lives in `MoveParams` and the durable `MoveRecord` (move_protocol.rs:68-82,
wallet-core/src/types.rs:482-501 (NOTE: wallet-core, not the 9-line wallet-fedimint re-export shim)), is copied into a one-gateway ledger field (ledger.rs:127-135,
journal.rs:2984-3002), and is reused on replay (executor.rs:234-274, 1942-1951). A global pin
currently wins unconditionally (executor.rs:277-305).
`move_protocol.rs` states it explicitly: "LN-only: v1 validates that the destination-selected
gateway also serves the source, giving the same internal-swap route as `Move`. No peg-out."

For `Move` that is fine -- routine rebalancing can decline and wait. For `Evacuate` it means a
dying federation with no shared gateway CANNOT be drained, which is the one case where refusing
costs money.

The primitives already exist and were exercised by hand: during the 2026-07-28 canary the wallet
paid an invoice minted by a DIFFERENT federation's gateway over real Lightning (walletd via
ostracoda paying an Afribit Kibera invoice via the Fedi/Henwen gateways). Only the move path
pins a single gateway.

## Required changes

1. `Evacuate` only. Do NOT extend `Move`: it keeps the swap-only path and its cheaper fee
   (measured: internal send leg 8,948 vs external 16,064 msat on 1,000,000).
2. STRICT ordering. Always attempt the shared-gateway swap first, because it is cheaper. Reach the
   Lightning hop ONLY when no gateway serves both ends. The hop must never pre-empt a VIABLE swap.
2b. DEFINE "no gateway serves both ends" precisely: registry presence is NOT the test. A shared
   gateway that is registered but dead or unpriceable must FALL THROUGH to the hop, or the
   evacuation livelocks in exactly the incident the hatch exists for. State what happens when the
   swap route's quote fails or times out.
3. The two-gateway shape: mint the invoice on the destination through a gateway that serves the
   DESTINATION, and pay it from the source through a gateway that serves the SOURCE. These are
   different gateways; the plan currently cannot express that.
4. No bar on the destination gateway -- take whichever the destination federation offers. During
   an evacuation a worse counterparty beats stranding the balance, and every additional gate is
   another way the escape hatch fails to open. Both legs stay hash-locked, so this adds no new
   trust (see ADR-0029 Consequences).
4b. RE-PRICE BOTH LEGS. Fresh evacuation sizing currently hardwires ONE gateway and the
   internal-swap `send_fee_minimum` discount (executor.rs:744, :805), which does not apply across
   two gateways, while the eventual pay recheck uses the invoice-aware source-gateway fee
   (executor.rs:1455, multi_client.rs:916). Pre-sizing must use the destination's receive fee plus
   the SOURCE gateway's EXTERNAL-send fee, or the hop is sized against a discount it will not get.
   Also update the one-gateway operator display (wallet-cli/src/main.rs:2997).
5. PERSIST THE ROUTE DURABLY and define replay. The record currently holds ONE gateway; a hop
   needs both identities, a route kind, operator-visible recording in the ledger, and explicit
   precedence against the global pin. DECIDE it explicitly rather than leaving it to the
   implementer -- today the pin returns unconditionally before any route search
   (executor.rs:341-343). State what a source-only pin, a destination-only pin, a shared pin, and
   an unusable pin each mean for route selection, and whether a pin may block the automatic
   fallback during an evacuation. Specify crash recovery at BOTH non-idempotent boundaries
   (cache-loss resume, and a crash after the receive but before the send), or a restart can route
   or pay differently than the first attempt while "one operation" still passes. The AC must
   therefore assert MORE than "exactly one operation": exactly one receive op, exactly one send op,
   one invoice / payment hash, the exact persisted gateway identities and route kind, and NO
   rerouting -- at BOTH killpoints (receive commit executor.rs:1353, send commit executor.rs:1500)
   with complete `MoveRecord` cache loss. Note op-log backfill currently DISCARDS each SDK
   operation's gateway (multi_client.rs:1222), so backfill must be extended too.
6. UPDATE THE DOCS THAT THIS CHANGE FALSIFIES: `docs/fedimint-mechanics.md` §5 (the "There is NO
   fallback when no shared gateway exists" passage) and `docs/roadmap-to-v1.md` (the one-gateway
   invariant bullet). Both have been pre-corrected to say the hop is decided-but-not-built; when
   the code lands they must say it is built.
7. Preserve the existing two-leg guarantees on the new route: idempotent replay, the gross-up so
   the destination nets the intended amount, the §15.7 committed-contract check, and honest
   terminal classification. The hop changes WHICH gateways are used, not the settlement model.

## Tests

MANDATORY, because the bead's own requirement 2b is otherwise untested and the evacuation can
still livelock while every other criterion passes:
- A shared gateway that is REGISTERED but dead / timing out / unpriceable falls through to the
  hop. Note the current quote path skips failures and can fall back to plain validation that
  re-selects the same unpriceable gateway (executor.rs:404, :441), so this test must be written
  red-first against that behaviour.
- Global-pin precedence, per the decision required below, with a case for each: source-only pin,
  destination-only pin, shared pin, and an unusable pin.

- With no gateway serving both federations, an evacuation SUCCEEDS via the hop and the destination
  is credited the intended net amount. This case LIVELOCKS today (`resolve_gateway` returns
`ExecError::Retryable`, executor.rs:350-356, explicitly documented "Retryable, NOT Permanent ...
never terminally Failed" at :333-335) -- it is retried every tick forever, NOT refused -- assert it is refused before
  the change, so the test is not vacuous.
- With a shared gateway available, the swap is chosen and the hop is NOT attempted; assert on the
  route actually taken, not merely on success, or a hop-always implementation passes.
- The hop path is idempotent under replay: re-driving the same evacuation yields ONE operation.
- A hop evacuation whose fee exceeds the (base + proportional) cap is refused.
- Live devimint gate: two federations with NO shared gateway, evacuation drains the source; exit
  codes captured, and one assertion deliberately broken first to prove the gate can fail.

## Gate prerequisites

The live gate needs TWO federations with DISJOINT gateway coverage. Per project experience
`dev-fed` starts ONE federation regardless of `--num-feds`, so two-fed runs need the existing
harness patch, PLUS new work to make a gateway serve only one federation. Budget these as part of
the bead; they are not incidental.

## Scope guard

Do NOT extend this to `Move`. Do NOT touch the per-federation balance cap -- ADR-0018 stands and
this route is best-effort, not a reliability guarantee, so nothing here justifies holding more per
federation. Do NOT add on-chain peg-out: ADR-0004 (lightning-only) holds and ADR-0018's
gateway-independent escape stays deferred. Do NOT add reputation, liquidity, or allowlist checks
on the destination gateway. Greenfield: no compatibility shims.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With no gateway serving both ends, an evacuation completes via a two-gateway Lightning hop
      and credits the intended net amount; the pre-change assertion must be that the intent stays non-terminal
      (Retryable/Pending) across N ticks -- NOT that it reaches a terminal Failed state, which
      never occurs.
- [ ] With a shared gateway present, the swap route is taken and the hop is not attempted --
      asserted on the route, not on success alone.
- [ ] Replaying a hop evacuation produces exactly one operation.
- [ ] A hop evacuation over the fee cap is refused.
- [ ] `Move` behaviour is unchanged, asserted by test.
- [ ] A live devimint gate drains a source federation with no shared gateway, is RUN not merely
      written, and is shown to go red when one assertion is deliberately broken.
